Epithelial Systems Biology Laboratory (ESBL)


RNA Polymerase II ChIP-seq and RNA-seq in mpkCCD Cells: Response to Vasopressin

--- These data were obtained in studies of mouse mpkCCD cells (clone 11) , a model of the collecting duct principal cell. These cells express the water channel aquaporin-2 (AQP2) and responds to the peptide hormone vasopressin with an increase in AQP2 trafficking to the apical plasma membrane and an increase in the abundance of the AQP2 protein. The study utilized deep sequencing methodology to profile mRNA abundance changes in response to the vasopressin analog, dDAVP, and to profile changes in binding of RNA polymerase II along the genome in response to dDAVP. Cells were treated with 0.1 nM dDAVP or vehicle control for 24 hr prior to observations. The ChIP-seq used an antibody to the large subunit of the RNA Polymerase II complex, viz. Polr2a. Full details of methodology and results interpretation are presented in a manuscript: Sandoval PC, Claxton JS, Lee JW, Saeed F, Hoffert JD, Knepper MA. Systems-level analysis reveals selective regulation of Aqp2 gene expression by vasopressin. Sci Rep. 2016 Oct 11;6:34863. PMID:27725713. Average values reported were from three pairs of samples for ChIP-seq and nine pairs for RNA-seq.

--- Definitions: norm., normalized; TPM, transcripts per million (a measure of mRNA abundance; see link). "Significant change in both" means that the ChIP-seq and TMP signals both exceed thresholds for 95% confidence interval for random variation based on control vs. control comparisons.

--- To reveal distribution of RNA Polymerase II binding along gene bodies of individual genes, hover over the gene symbol. TSS, transcription start site; EAG, end of annotated gene.

--- Created by Pablo Sandoval, J'neka Claxton, Fahad Saeed, and Mark Knepper. Please address questions or comments to: knep@helix.nih.gov. Database created: December, 2015 (download data)
